name: revenue_sdk
_comment_app_type: Both personas now get a real page install. manager: templates/pages/manager/income -> lib/presentation/pages/income (ManagerIncomeRoute, CupertinoRoute). driver: templates/pages/driver/income -> the same host path (DriverIncomeRoute, MaterialRoute - matching zones_sdk's DriverDeliveryZoneRoute convention); the driver template keeps ${package} imports into the host's own services/components/styles and its app-owned lib/application/statistics layer (which already talks to this SDK's CourierStatisticsRepositoryFacade), and its chart still uses the host's charts_flutter dependency - the template compiles in the HOST package, so charts_flutter stays in the host pubspec, not here. Driver also keeps the directly-imported lib/src/driver/ slice, and declaring both personas keeps the matching lib/src/ role folder alive through sdk_composer.py's strip_unused_role_folders. A non-manager, non-driver app that composes revenue_sdk still gets the package and its DI registration, but no pages and no role-specific code kept in cache. Requires .rokct/config/app_type to contain the matching value - resolve_app_type() returns None without it and no flavour block fires. Both installs are whole-directory copies, so verify lib/presentation/pages/income actually lands after composing.
_comment_routes: Each persona's income_page.dart carries @RoutePage(name: '...IncomeRoute') (ManagerIncomeRoute / DriverIncomeRoute) and installs into the HOST's lib/, so auto_route codegen generates the route class there - which is why these routes import the installed page directly via ${package} rather than needing a *_route_pages.dart wrapper the way auth_sdk does.
